subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should OpenClaw core define a bounded Telegram/ACP invariant for visible success claims that are not backed by matching tool/result evidence, or should broad claim verification remain a plugin/ClawHub policy?
rationale: Current main only warns on the narrower message-tool-only private-final class; arbitrary claimed side effects cross privacy, retry, delivery, plugin-boundary, and product-default decisions that automation should not choose.

options.title: Define bounded core policy
options.body: Require live Telegram/ACP reproduction and implement a narrow source-turn diagnostic or fail-closed invariant for visible success claims with no matching tool/result evidence.

options.title: Keep broad verification in plugins
options.body: Limit core to message delivery invariants and route claim-vs-ledger enforcement to plugin hooks or ClawHub policy packages.

options.title: Document current boundary only
options.body: Clarify that OpenClaw does not guarantee semantic verification of arbitrary success claims and rely on operators or plugins for post-tool-use checks.

recommendation.title: Define bounded core policy
recommendation.body: Require live Telegram/ACP reproduction and implement a narrow source-turn diagnostic or fail-closed invariant for visible success claims with no matching tool/result evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The related #86463 source-reply policy and #68051 plugin-boundary decisions point to this person for the product-boundary choice.
